## Acceptance check: ingest, transcript-intake and second-brain-query (read-only, 2026-10-10)

This was a routing and retrieval check. Nothing was ingested, written, installed or delegated, and I ran no shell commands or live APIs. I read no student records.

### Skill project paths

| Skill | Active project path | Catalog copy |
|---|---|---|
| `ingest` | `C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os\.claude\skills\ingest\SKILL.md` | `skills\claude\ingest\SKILL.md` |
| `transcript-intake` | `.claude\skills\transcript-intake\SKILL.md` | `skills\claude\transcript-intake\SKILL.md` |
| `second-brain-query` | `.claude\skills\second-brain-query\SKILL.md` | `skills\claude\second-brain-query\SKILL.md` |

- **Dispatcher:** the user-level `ingest` at `C:\Users\Joshu\.claude\skills\ingest` is only a dispatcher. It points to the project copy above.
- **Schema:** `system\schema\llm-wiki.md` exists and I read it.
- **Missing skills:** none.
- **Blocked reads:** none.

### Routing

| Input | Route | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| AI article clip | `ingest` → Clips: `raw/inbox/`, SHA-256 dedupe, archive to `raw/sources/clips/<slug>/`, source summary in `wiki/sources/`, AI content filed through `references/ai-workspace/index.md`, then `wiki/index.md` and `wiki/log.md`. | PASS |
| Public video without captions | `ingest` → Clips: get native captions or an authorized transcription route. It never goes to student `transcript-intake`. If acquisition is blocked, report the missing transcript and don't infer content. | PASS |
| Student transcript lookup | `transcript-intake`: a lookup stays read-only and narrow. It uses `gws` for Calendar and Drive, matches guests by email, and checks both attached and unattached Gemini Docs. `ingest` explicitly hands this route off. | PASS |

I did not exercise the live `gws` and Calendar path, so that part of the lookup route is untested.

### Retrieval: what the saved Claude JavaScript video suggested Joshua could reuse

I found the page by searching `wiki/index.md` for "javascript", then read the source page and the dated section of the video options page. The source page is [`claude-now-does-video-free-javascript.md`](C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os\wiki\sources\claude-now-does-video-free-javascript.md). The comparison is in [`VIDEO-GENERATION-OPTIONS-2026-09-09.md`](C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os\wiki\VIDEO-GENERATION-OPTIONS-2026-09-09.md) under "Added 2026-10-10".

Everything below is the narrator's claim (Chase AI). It has been captured and read, not tested here.

**A second route alongside Remotion.**
- Claude writes a function that turns a time `t` into a picture.
- Playwright's headless browser draws 60 frames per second.
- FFmpeg stitches the frames into an MP4.
- The narrator calls it "essentially free", meaning Claude usage only.
- The page treats this as complementary to the existing Remotion recommendation, not a replacement.

**Habits the saved page says would apply to either route and cost nothing to adopt:**
- Ask for a storyboard of scene frames before any code runs.
- State the length, aspect ratio and audio route in the prompt.
- End the prompt with "pull a contact sheet, look at it, fix, re-render, repeat".
- Supply the narration first and time the visuals to it.
- Use a reference image or video to borrow style.

**Qualifications the pages preserve:**
- **Timings:** the 20 minute, 30 minute and 8 hour figures for a 15-second showreel are his and unverified.
- **Transcript quality:** names such as "ultra code", "Fable 5.1" and "skillery.dev" come from captions and should be checked against the video before anyone quotes them.
- **Skill unknown:** the skill he distributes has no URL in the clip, so its name, repository and licence are unknown. It can't be assessed or installed from this source.
- **Promotion:** the video has a sponsor segment and a plug for his paid community.
- **Local prerequisites:** FFmpeg is recorded as installed. Playwright and faster-whisper are not recorded.
- **Untested:** whether the plain route beats Remotion on a real RRC or conditional lesson is open.
- **Status:** the source page marks it "captured", not evaluated or tested.

Retrieval was bounded: one index search, two page reads, one targeted search. I did not read the whole index and did not open the raw source.

### Verdict

- **Routing: PASS.** All three routes resolve correctly with no missing dependencies.
- **Retrieval: PASS.** The answer came from compiled pages, with the evidence chain visible (source page → archived clip provenance and hash) and the source-claim qualifications kept.

This was a diagnostic and retrieval check on already-saved knowledge. It is not a new-source ingestion: nothing was hashed, archived, compiled, indexed or logged. I did not open the raw clip or its `PROVENANCE.md`, so I did not re-check the SHA-256 the source page cites.
